verdict.justification: B is preferable because its payroll exception is consistent with the supplied April sources: the $236,500 payroll accrual plus $20,500 special IT accrual totals $257,000, exceeding the trial balance liability of $141,033 by $115,967. A instead reports a difference of $177,467, materially misstating a key CFO review item. Both deliverables clearly identify the missing AP source, prepaid insurance discrepancy, unsupported Division 12 receivable, and assumed funding allocation, while documenting the CFO-reserved tabs as excluded. B also lists Loan I and Loan II separately in the TOC and explicitly flags the Loan I rate assumption, making navigation and review more precise. A offers useful additional review support through its listed “Schedule-to-GL Tie-Out” tab, but that advantage does not outweigh the payroll accuracy issue.

decisive_issues.issue: Payroll reconciliation difference does not agree with the supplied April accruals and trial balance.
Correctly quantifies the payroll accrual discrepancy at $115,967.
Explicitly flags the Loan I interest-rate assumption for CFO review.
